summary: Mobile hotspot on 5th floor causes asymmetric routing that drops VPN-originated traffic to internal services intermittently
description:
Issue summary: Multiple employees on the 5th floor report intermittent failures reaching internal services (e.g., internal registry, metrics, and auth services) while connected to the corporate SSID and the company VPN. Symptoms appear when a nearby personal mobile hotspot (identified by device MACs ending in :A3:B2) is active and clients are simultaneously connected to both Wi-Fi and the hotspot (phone tethering).

Impact: Affects ~8-12 users on floor 5 during peak periods. Causes service access errors (timeout, TCP RST) for internal infra services; developer workflows and monitoring alerts are impacted. No customer-facing outages.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 08:45: First user report in #it-support. Intermittent 502/timeout from internal registry.
- 2026-03-09 09:12 Initial log correlation shows VPN tunnels established but service replies not reaching client.
- 2026-03-10 10:00 Wireless controller logs show client is connected to corporate-SSID; ARP and DHCP entries show frequent default-gateway change for some clients.
- 2026-03-10 14:30 Wireshark capture from affected client shows SYN/ACKs from internal service returning to public hotspot IP (asymmetric path) and NAT hairpin failures.

Observed behavior: When personal hotspot is active, some clients choose the hotspot's upstream path for return traffic despite sending via VPN. Packet captures show outbound packets encapsulated by VPN to the datacenter, but the return path uses hotspot's public IP (likely because of source address selection or local policy), causing stateful firewall/NAT to drop or misroute replies. Symptoms include TCP connection reset, application-level timeouts, and occasional VPN rekey/teardown after repeated failures.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a laptop joined to corporate SSID, start company VPN and confirm access to internal service (curl http://internal-registry:5000/ping).
2) On nearby phone, enable mobile hotspot and connect the same laptop to the hotspot simultaneously (test cases seen when laptop maintains both Wi-Fi and hotspot associations via different radios or USB tethering).
3) Re-run curl to internal service; observe intermittent failures and capture packets with tcpdump.
4) Compare traceroute and tcpdump to confirm asymmetric return path via hotspot external IP.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Client OS/source address selection uses non-VPN interface for some return traffic (Windows metric or multipath behavior).
- NAC/Edge firewall stateful NAT expects symmetric path; hotspot introduces asymmetry.
- AP/controller roaming or client sticky rules causing local route preference swings.

Findings so far:
- Packet captures confirm return traffic leaving the datacenter to the hotspot public IP rather than the VPN source.
- DHCP lease events on affected clients show occasional default gateway re-evaluation when hotspot is active.
- Wireless controller shows no immediate configuration anomalies for corporate-SSID; guest/guest-vlan isolation appears intact.
- No config changes were rolled out in the timeframe, making a local client/network interaction the likely trigger.

Temporary mitigations tested:
- Instructed users to disable phone hotspot while on corporate SSID: immediate improvement.
- Applied a quick NAC rule to de-prioritize clients with active tethering flags (RADIUS vendor attribute) on floor 5 for 24h; reduced incident count by ~70%.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Initial user reports collected from #it-support and direct Slack DMs. Attaching sample client IPs and timestamps.

Liam Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Captured tcpdump from an affected laptop and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/INT-130218/client-capture-20260310.pcap). Observed SYN/ACKs returning to hotspot IP. Suspect asymmetric routing due to source address selection.

Network Eng (Priya Reddy) 2026-03-11: Confirmed controller logs show client retains corporate-SSID association while tethered in some USB-tether cases. Will review AP roaming/power settings and client metric policies.

SRE (Marcus Li) 2026-03-11: Raised PR to update firewall NAT timeouts and add heuristic allowing return traffic to hotspot IP for short windows (PR link in related_github_prs). This is a stopgap and not ideal.
Liam Chen 2026-03-12: Rolled temporary NAC rule to isolate tethered clients on floor-5 for 24 hours. Monitoring for recurrence. Planning long-term fix with wireless team.
resolution: Workaround applied: NAC rule deployed to reduce likelihood of asymmetric routing by isolating tethered clients on floor 5; users advised to disable personal hotspots while on corporate network. Long-term plan: wireless team to adjust AP power/steering and implement controller-level tethering detection and enforcement; network team to evaluate route preference and Windows metric tuning documentation. Follow-ups: schedule change in controller to enforce guest uplink isolation on APs serving floor 5 and roll firewall NAT/window improvements (tracked in related_github_prs).
next_steps:
1) Wireless team (Priya) to test AP power/roaming adjustments in staging (target: 2026-03-18).
2) SRE to evaluate NAT/window changes and produce rollback plan (target: 2026-03-16).
3) Update internal KB with recommended client settings to avoid dual uplinks (target: 2026-03-15).
4) Re-assess after 72h of NAC rule and collect any remaining captures for deeper analysis.
